sanskrit: śūrāś ca kṛtavidyāś ca spardhante ca parasparam nityaṃ ca samare rājan vijigīṣanti mānavān
english: They are heroes, masters of their craft, and they vie with one another; ever, O king, do they long to conquer their fellow men in battle.

sanskrit: karṇena vijitā rājan duḥśāsanam anuvratāḥ etāṃs tu vāsudevo 'pi rathodārān praśaṃsati
english: Subdued by Karṇa, O king, they are devoted followers of Duḥśāsana; even Vāsudeva praises these noble chariot-warriors.

sanskrit: satataṃ priyakāmāś ca karṇasyaite vaśe sthitāḥ tasyaiva vacanād rājan nivṛttāḥ śvetavāhanāt
english: Always eager to please, they stand under Karṇa's command; it was at his word, O king, that they turned back from him whose steeds are white.

sanskrit: te na kṣatā na ca śrāntā dṛḍhāvaraṇakārmukāḥ madarthaṃ viṣṭhitā nūnaṃ dhārtarāṣṭrasya śāsanāt
english: Unwounded and unwearied, with sturdy armor and bows, they wait now on my account, surely by the command of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son.

sanskrit: etān pramathya saṃgrāme priyārthaṃ tava kaurava prayāsyāmi tataḥ paścāt padavīṃ savyasācinaḥ
english: Crushing these in battle for your pleasure, O Kaurava, I shall afterward set out upon the track of Savyasācin.

sanskrit: yāṃs tv etān aparān rājan nāgān saptaśatāni ca prekṣase varmasaṃchannān kirātaiḥ samadhiṣṭhitān
english: And those others you behold, O king—seven hundred elephants sheathed in armor, mounted by Kirātas—

sanskrit: kirātarājo yān prādād gṛhītaḥ savyasācinā svalaṃkṛtāṃs tathā preṣyān icchañ jīvitam ātmanaḥ
english: these the king of the Kirātas, taken captive by Savyasācin, gave as servants, well adorned, desiring to keep his own life.

sanskrit: āsann ete purā rājaṃs tava karmakarā dṛḍham tvām evādya yuyutsante paśya kālasya paryayam
english: Formerly, O king, these were your steadfast servants; today they are eager to fight against you. Behold the turning of time!

sanskrit: teṣām ete mahāmātrāḥ kirātā yuddhadurmadāḥ hastiśikṣāvidaś caiva sarve caivāgniyonayaḥ
english: Their mahouts are these Kirātas, frenzied for battle, skilled in the lore of elephants, and all of them sprung from fire.

sanskrit: ete vinirjitāḥ sarve saṃgrāme savyasācinā madartham adya saṃyattā duryodhanavaśānugāḥ
english: All these were vanquished in battle by Savyasācin; today, arrayed against me, they follow the will of Duryodhana.

sanskrit: etān bhittvā śarai rājan kirātān yuddhadurmadān saindhavasya vadhe yuktam anuyāsyāmi pāṇḍavam
english: Having shattered these battle-maddened Kirātas with my arrows, O king, I shall follow the Pāṇḍava, intent on the slaying of the Saindhava.

sanskrit: ye tv ete sumahānāgā añjanasya kulodbhavāḥ karkaśāś ca vinītāś ca prabhinnakaraṭāmukhāḥ
english: And those mighty elephants born of the line of Añjana—rugged yet well trained, their cheeks and trunks streaming with rut—

sanskrit: jāmbūnadamayaiḥ sarvair varmabhiḥ suvibhūṣitāḥ labdhalakṣyā raṇe rājann airāvaṇasamā yudhi
english: all richly adorned with armor of pure gold, unerring of aim in battle, O king, the equals of Airāvaṇa in war—

sanskrit: uttarāt parvatād ete tīkṣṇair dasyubhir āsthitāḥ karkaśaiḥ pravarair yodhaiḥ kārṣṇāyasatanucchadaiḥ
english: these, from the northern mountain, are ridden by fierce marauders, rugged and matchless warriors clad in coats of black iron.

sanskrit: santi goyonayaś cātra santi vānarayonayaḥ anekayonayaś cānye tathā mānuṣayonayaḥ
english: Among them are some of cattle-born stock and some of monkey-born stock, and others of manifold origin, and some of human origin as well.

sanskrit: anīkam asatām etad dhūmavarṇam udīryate mlecchānāṃ pāpakartṝṇāṃ himavaddurgavāsinām
english: Smoke-colored, this host of the wicked rises up—of Mlecchas, doers of evil, dwellers in the fastnesses of Himavat.

sanskrit: etad duryodhano labdhvā samagraṃ nāgamaṇḍalam kṛpaṃ ca saumadattiṃ ca droṇaṃ ca rathināṃ varam
english: Having gained this whole circle of elephants, Duryodhana, driven by his doom, holds in contempt Kṛpa, the son of Somadatta, Droṇa best of chariot-warriors,

sanskrit: sindhurājaṃ tathā karṇam avamanyata pāṇḍavān kṛtārtham atha cātmānaṃ manyate kālacoditaḥ
english: the king of the Sindhus, and Karṇa too, and disdains the Pāṇḍavas, and reckons his own purpose already accomplished.

sanskrit: te ca sarve 'nusaṃprāptā mama nārācagocaram na vimokṣyanti kaunteya yady api syur manojavāḥ
english: And all these, once come within range of my iron shafts, shall not escape, O son of Kuntī, even were they swift as thought.

sanskrit: tena saṃbhāvitā nityaṃ paravīryopajīvinā vināśam upayāsyanti maccharaughanipīḍitāḥ
english: Ever favored by him who lives upon the valor of others, they shall go to their destruction, beaten down by the floods of my arrows.

sanskrit: ye tv ete rathino rājan dṛśyante kāñcanadhvajāḥ ete durvāraṇā nāma kāmbojā yadi te śrutāḥ
english: And those chariot-warriors you see, O king, with banners of gold—these are the Kāmbojas called Durvāraṇa, if you have heard of them.

sanskrit: śūrāś ca kṛtavidyāś ca dhanurvede ca niṣṭhitāḥ saṃhatāś ca bhṛśaṃ hy ete anyonyasya hitaiṣiṇaḥ
english: Heroes, masters of their craft, accomplished in the science of the bow, tightly knit together, each seeking the welfare of the others.

sanskrit: akṣauhiṇyaś ca saṃrabdhā dhārtarāṣṭrasya bhārata yattā madarthaṃ tiṣṭhanti kuruvīrābhirakṣitāḥ
english: Whole armies of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son, roused to fury, O Bhārata, stand ready on my account, guarded round by the Kuru heroes.

sanskrit: apramattā mahārāja mām eva pratyupasthitāḥ tāṃs tv ahaṃ pramathiṣyāmi tṛṇānīva hutāśanaḥ
english: Vigilant, O great king, they have ranged themselves against me; yet I shall consume them as fire consumes blades of grass.

sanskrit: tasmāt sarvān upāsaṅgān sarvopakaraṇāni ca rathe kurvantu me rājan yathāvad rathakalpakāḥ
english: Therefore, O king, let the chariot-fitters set in proper order upon my car all the quivers and all the equipment.

sanskrit: asmiṃs tu khalu saṃgrāme grāhyaṃ vividham āyudham yathopadiṣṭam ācāryaiḥ kāryaḥ pañcaguṇo rathaḥ
english: In this battle indeed weapons of many kinds must be taken up; as the teachers have prescribed, the chariot must be fivefold furnished.

sanskrit: kāmbojair hi sameṣyāmi kruddhair āśīviṣopamaiḥ nānāśastrasamāvāpair vividhāyudhayodhibhiḥ
english: For I shall meet the Kāmbojas, enraged and like venomous serpents, masters of many missiles, warriors of manifold weapons.

sanskrit: kirātaiś ca sameṣyāmi viṣakalpaiḥ prahāribhiḥ lālitaiḥ satataṃ rājñā duryodhanahitaiṣibhiḥ
english: And I shall meet the Kirātas, smiters like poison, ever cherished by the king and seeking Duryodhana's good.

sanskrit: śakaiś cāpi sameṣyāmi śakratulyaparākramaiḥ agnikalpair durādharṣaiḥ pradīptair iva pāvakaiḥ
english: And I shall meet the Śakas too, in prowess the equals of Śakra, like fire itself, unassailable, blazing as kindled flames.

sanskrit: tathānyair vividhair yodhaiḥ kālakalpair durāsadaiḥ sameṣyāmi raṇe rājan bahubhir yuddhadurmadaiḥ
english: And with many other warriors of every kind, like Death itself and hard to withstand, I shall close in battle, O king—with hosts of them, frenzied for war.

sanskrit: tasmād vai vājino mukhyā viśrāntāḥ śubhalakṣaṇāḥ upāvṛttāś ca pītāś ca punar yujyantu me rathe
english: Therefore let my chief horses, rested and of auspicious marks, watered and given drink, be yoked again to my chariot.

sanskrit: tasya sarvān upāsaṅgān sarvopakaraṇāni ca rathe prāsthāpayad rājā śastrāṇi vividhāni ca
english: For him the king had set upon the chariot all the quivers and all the equipment and weapons of many kinds.

sanskrit: tatas tān sarvato muktvā sadaśvāṃś caturo janāḥ rasavat pāyayām āsuḥ pānaṃ madasamīriṇam
english: Then the men, unyoking on every side the four fine steeds, gave them a savory draught to drink, a brew that quickened their spirit.

sanskrit: pītopavṛttān snātāṃś ca jagdhānnān samalaṃkṛtān vinītaśalyāṃs turagāṃś caturo hemamālinaḥ
english: The four horses, watered and turned out, bathed, fed with grain, well adorned, their thorns and burrs removed, garlanded with gold,

sanskrit: tān yattān rukmavarṇābhān vinītāñ śīghragāminaḥ saṃhṛṣṭamanaso 'vyagrān vidhivat kalpite rathe
english: these, ready and gleaming gold of hue, well broken, swift of foot, glad of heart and unflustered—they yoked to the chariot duly made ready,

sanskrit: mahādhvajena siṃhena hemakesaramālinā saṃvṛte ketanair hemair maṇividrumacitritaiḥ pāṇḍurābhraprakāśābhiḥ patākābhir alaṃkṛte
english: a chariot crowned with a great lion-standard maned in gold, hung about with golden ensigns inlaid with gems and coral, and adorned with banners bright as pale clouds,

sanskrit: hemadaṇḍocchritacchatre bahuśastraparicchade yojayām āsa vidhivad dhemabhāṇḍavibhūṣitān
english: a chariot with a parasol raised on a golden staff and arrayed with many weapons—to it they yoked them duly, decked in golden trappings.

sanskrit: dārukasyānujo bhrātā sūtas tasya priyaḥ sakhā nyavedayad rathaṃ yuktaṃ vāsavasyeva mātaliḥ
english: Dāruka's younger brother, his charioteer and dear friend, announced the yoked chariot, as Mātali does to Vāsava.

sanskrit: tataḥ snātaḥ śucir bhūtvā kṛtakautukamaṅgalaḥ snātakānāṃ sahasrasya svarṇaniṣkān adāpayat āśīrvādaiḥ pariṣvaktaḥ sātyakiḥ śrīmatāṃ varaḥ
english: Then, bathed and made pure, the rites of good omen performed, Sātyaki, best of the glorious, caused golden coins to be given to a thousand graduate Brahmins, and was enfolded in their blessings.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa madhuparkārhaḥ pītvā kailāvataṃ madhu lohitākṣo babhau tatra madavihvalalocanaḥ
english: Then, worthy of the honey-offering, having drunk the mead of Kailāvata, the red-eyed one shone there, his eyes swimming with its potency.

sanskrit: ālabhya vīrakāṃsyaṃ ca harṣeṇa mahatānvitaḥ dviguṇīkṛtatejā hi prajvalann iva pāvakaḥ utsaṅge dhanur ādāya saśaraṃ rathināṃ varaḥ
english: Touching the hero's bowl, filled with great gladness, his splendor redoubled, blazing like fire, the best of chariot-warriors took up upon his lap his bow with its arrows,

sanskrit: kṛtasvastyayano vipraiḥ kavacī samalaṃkṛtaḥ lājair gandhais tathā mālyaiḥ kanyābhiś cābhinanditaḥ
english: the rites of blessing done for him by the Brahmins—armored, well adorned, greeted with parched grain, fragrances, and garlands, and by maidens.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhirasya caraṇāv abhivādya kṛtāñjaliḥ tena mūrdhany upāghrāta āruroha mahāratham
english: Having saluted the feet of Yudhiṣṭhira with joined palms, and kissed by him upon the head, he mounted his great chariot.

sanskrit: tatas te vājino hṛṣṭāḥ supuṣṭā vātaraṃhasaḥ ajayyā jaitram ūhus taṃ vikurvantaḥ sma saindhavāḥ
english: Then those Saindhava steeds, glad and well nourished, swift as the wind and unconquerable, drew that conqueror along, prancing as they went.

sanskrit: atha harṣaparītāṅgaḥ sātyakir bhīmam abravīt tvaṃ bhīma rakṣa rājānam etat kāryatamaṃ hi te
english: Then Sātyaki, his every limb flooded with joy, said to Bhīma: "Do you, Bhīma, guard the king; that is the foremost of your duties.

sanskrit: ahaṃ bhittvā pravekṣyāmi kālapakvam idaṃ balam āyatyāṃ ca tadātve ca śreyo rājño 'bhirakṣaṇam
english: I shall break through and enter this host now ripened for doom; both for the time to come and for the present, the guarding of the king is the greater good."

sanskrit: jānīṣe mama vīryaṃ tvaṃ tava cāham ariṃdama tasmād bhīma nivartasva mama ced icchasi priyam
english: "You know my valor, and I yours, O scourge of foes; therefore, Bhīma, turn back, if you wish me well."

sanskrit: tathoktaḥ sātyakiṃ prāha vraja tvaṃ kāryasiddhaye ahaṃ rājñaḥ kariṣyāmi rakṣāṃ puruṣasattama
english: So addressed, he said to Sātyaki: "Go you to the accomplishing of your task; I shall keep guard over the king, O best of men."

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ pratyuvāca bhīmasenaṃ sa mādhavaḥ gaccha gaccha drutaṃ pārtha dhruvo 'dya vijayo mama
english: Thus addressed, that Mādhava replied to Bhīmasena: "Go, go swiftly, O Pārtha; sure is my victory this day.

sanskrit: yan me snigdho 'nuraktaś ca tvam adya vaśagaḥ sthitaḥ nimittāni ca dhanyāni yathā bhīma vadanti me
english: For you, loving and devoted, stand today obedient to me, and the omens speak of good fortune to me, O Bhīma.

sanskrit: nihate saindhave pāpe pāṇḍavena mahātmanā pariṣvajiṣye rājānaṃ dharmātmānaṃ na saṃśayaḥ
english: When the wicked Saindhava is slain by the great-souled Pāṇḍava, I shall embrace the king, that soul of righteousness—of this there is no doubt."

sanskrit: etāvad uktvā bhīmaṃ tu visṛjya ca mahāmanāḥ saṃpraikṣat tāvakaṃ sainyaṃ vyāghro mṛgagaṇān iva
english: Having said this much to Bhīma and taken his leave of him, the great-spirited one surveyed your army as a tiger surveys the herds of deer.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā pravivikṣantaṃ sainyaṃ tava janādhipa bhūya evābhavan mūḍhaṃ subhṛśaṃ cāpy akampata
english: Seeing him about to enter, O lord of men, your army was bewildered yet more and trembled exceedingly.

sanskrit: tataḥ prayātaḥ sahasā sainyaṃ tava sa sātyakiḥ didṛkṣur arjunaṃ rājan dharmarājasya śāsanāt
english: Then Sātyaki advanced at once against your host, longing to behold Arjuna, O king, at the command of the Dharma King.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca prayāte tava sainyaṃ tu yuyudhāne yuyutsayā dharmarājo mahārāja svenānīkena saṃvṛtaḥ prāyād droṇarathaprepsur yuyudhānasya pṛṣṭhataḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: When Yuyudhāna had advanced against your army in his eagerness for battle, the Dharma King, O great king, encircled by his own troops, set forth behind Yuyudhāna, seeking to reach Droṇa's chariot.

sanskrit: tataḥ pāñcālarājasya putraḥ samaradurmadaḥ prākrośat pāṇḍavānīke vasudānaś ca pārthivaḥ
english: Then the son of the Pāñcāla king, frenzied in battle, and the prince Vasudāna cried aloud within the Pāṇḍava host:

sanskrit: āgacchata praharata drutaṃ viparidhāvata yathā sukhena gaccheta sātyakir yuddhadurmadaḥ
english: "Come on, strike, run swiftly hither and yon, so that Sātyaki, frenzied for battle, may pass through with ease.

sanskrit: mahārathā hi bahavo yatiṣyanty asya nirjaye iti bruvanto vegena samāpetur balaṃ tava
english: For many great chariot-warriors will strive for his defeat." So saying, they fell with fury upon your host.

sanskrit: vayaṃ pratijigīṣantas tatra tān samabhidrutāḥ tataḥ śabdo mahān āsīd yuyudhānarathaṃ prati
english: We, seeking to overcome them, rushed against them there; then a mighty din arose about Yuyudhāna's chariot.

sanskrit: prakampyamānā mahatī tava putrasya vāhinī sātvatena mahārāja śatadhābhivyadīryata
english: The great army of your son, shaken by the Sātvata, O great king, was rent asunder a hundredfold.

sanskrit: tasyāṃ vidīryamāṇāyāṃ śineḥ pautro mahārathaḥ sapta vīrān maheṣvāsān agrānīke vyapothayat
english: As it was being torn apart, the grandson of Śini, that great chariot-warrior, crushed seven heroic, mighty archers in the forefront of the host.

sanskrit: te bhītā mṛdyamānāś ca pramṛṣṭā dīrghabāhunā āyodhanaṃ jahur vīrā dṛṣṭvā tam atimānuṣam
english: Terrified, ground down and swept away by the long-armed one, those heroes abandoned the field of battle, seeing him more than human.

sanskrit: rathair vimathitākṣaiś ca bhagnanīḍaiś ca māriṣa cakrair vimathitaiś chinnair dhvajaiś ca vinipātitaiḥ
english: With chariots whose axles were broken and whose frames were shattered, O sire, with wheels crushed and split, and banners cast down,

sanskrit: anukarṣaiḥ patākābhiḥ śirastrāṇaiḥ sakāñcanaiḥ bāhubhiś candanādigdhaiḥ sāṅgadaiś ca viśāṃ pate
english: with chariot-poles, pennants, golden helmets, and arms smeared with sandal and braced with armlets, O lord of the people,

sanskrit: hastihastopamaiś cāpi bhujagābhogasaṃnibhaiḥ ūrubhiḥ pṛthivī channā manujānāṃ narottama
english: and with the thighs of men, like the trunks of elephants, like the coils of serpents, was the earth strewn over, O best of men.

sanskrit: śaśāṅkasaṃnikāśaiś ca vadanaiś cārukuṇḍalaiḥ patitair vṛṣabhākṣāṇāṃ babhau bhārata medinī
english: With the fallen faces of bull-eyed men, faces like the moon and adorned with lovely earrings, the earth shone, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: gajaiś ca bahudhā chinnaiḥ śayānaiḥ parvatopamaiḥ rarājātibhṛśaṃ bhūmir vikīrṇair iva parvataiḥ
english: And with elephants hewn in many pieces, lying like mountains, the ground gleamed exceedingly, as though strewn with shattered hills.

sanskrit: tapanīyamayair yoktrair muktājālavibhūṣitaiḥ uraśchadair vicitraiś ca vyaśobhanta turaṃgamāḥ gatasattvā mahīṃ prāpya pramṛṣṭā dīrghabāhunā
english: With harness of bright gold, decked with nets of pearl, and with bright-figured breast-plates, the horses gleamed—lifeless now, fallen to the earth, swept down by the long-armed one.

sanskrit: nānāvidhāni sainyāni tava hatvā tu sātvataḥ praviṣṭas tāvakaṃ sainyaṃ drāvayitvā camūṃ bhṛśam
english: Having slain your troops of many kinds, the Sātvata pierced deep into your host, and put your army to violent flight.

sanskrit: tatas tenaiva mārgeṇa yena yāto dhanaṃjayaḥ iyeṣa sātyakir gantuṃ tato droṇena vāritaḥ
english: Then Sātyaki sought to go by that very road by which Dhanaṃjaya had passed; but he was checked by Droṇa.

sanskrit: bharadvājaṃ samāsādya yuyudhānas tu māriṣa nābhyavartata saṃkruddho velām iva jalāśayaḥ
english: Coming upon the son of Bharadvāja, Yuyudhāna, O sire, though enraged, advanced no farther—as the sea does not pass its shore.

sanskrit: nivārya tu raṇe droṇo yuyudhānaṃ mahāratham vivyādha niśitair bāṇaiḥ pañcabhir marmabhedibhiḥ
english: Having stayed in battle Yuyudhāna, that great chariot-warrior, Droṇa pierced him with five sharp, vital-rending arrows.

sanskrit: sātyakis tu raṇe droṇaṃ rājan vivyādha saptabhiḥ hemapuṅkhaiḥ śilādhautaiḥ kaṅkabarhiṇavājitaiḥ
english: But Sātyaki in the fight pierced Droṇa, O king, with seven shafts of golden notch, whetted on stone, fledged with heron and peacock feathers.

sanskrit: taṃ ṣaḍbhiḥ sāyakair droṇaḥ sāśvayantāram ārdayat sa taṃ na mamṛṣe droṇaṃ yuyudhāno mahārathaḥ
english: With six arrows Droṇa struck him, together with his horses and his driver; but Yuyudhāna, that great chariot-warrior, would not brook this from Droṇa.

sanskrit: siṃhanādaṃ tataḥ kṛtvā droṇaṃ vivyādha sātyakiḥ daśabhiḥ sāyakaiś cānyaiḥ ṣaḍbhir aṣṭābhir eva ca
english: Then, with a lion's roar, Sātyaki pierced Droṇa with ten arrows, and with six others, and with eight again.

sanskrit: yuyudhānaḥ punar droṇaṃ vivyādha daśabhiḥ śaraiḥ ekena sārathiṃ cāsya caturbhiś caturo hayān dhvajam ekena bāṇena vivyādha yudhi māriṣa
english: Yuyudhāna pierced Droṇa once more with ten arrows, and his charioteer with one, and his four horses with four, and with a single shaft he pierced his banner in the fight, O sire.

sanskrit: taṃ droṇaḥ sāśvayantāraṃ sarathadhvajam āśugaiḥ tvaran prācchādayad bāṇaiḥ śalabhānām iva vrajaiḥ
english: Him, with his horses and driver, his chariot and banner, Droṇa swiftly covered with his fleet arrows, as with swarms of locusts.

sanskrit: tathaiva yuyudhāno 'pi droṇaṃ bahubhir āśugaiḥ prācchādayad asaṃbhrāntas tato droṇa uvāca ha
english: And in the same way Yuyudhāna too, unflinching, covered Droṇa with many fleet arrows; then Droṇa spoke:

sanskrit: tavācāryo raṇaṃ hitvā gataḥ kāpuruṣo yathā yudhyamānaṃ hi māṃ hitvā pradakṣiṇam avartata
english: "Your teacher has left the battle and gone, like a coward; for he forsook me while I fought, and turned aside, keeping me on his right.

sanskrit: tvaṃ hi me yudhyato nādya jīvan mokṣyasi mādhava yadi māṃ tvaṃ raṇe hitvā na yāsy ācāryavad drutam
english: You shall not escape me with your life today while I do battle, O Mādhava—unless you too forsake me in the fight and flee in haste, as your teacher did."
